**The pattern:** Medicare and Medicaid was the busiest beat this run — 26 items from eight sources, cohesion 0.03 — and it is not one story; the items share a tag, not a subject. Four of its newest pieces do, however, describe one thing when read together, and that reading is mine rather than something the beat did on its own: the price and the paperwork of disagreeing with Medicare in CY 2027. The Federal Register notice published 09/16/26 sets the amount-in-controversy thresholds for administrative law judge hearings and judicial review, giving $200 as a CY 2027 threshold, effective for requests filed on or after 01/01/27. All of these are confirmed gaps against the 114 monitored publishers.

**Why it matters:** A dollar floor on appeals decides which denials are contestable at all. The small, recurring denials an older adult actually receives — a supply order, a piece of equipment, a single visit — sit close to or below a $200 threshold, which means the cheapest denials are the ones that never reach a judge. On the other side of the same system, the CY 2027 payment rules and the HCPCS codes that determine whether an item is covered in the first place are being set in comment files and a public meeting, and the record of who showed up is now published: one advocacy organization's comments, one caregiving coalition's response, and 111 signatures on immigrant eligibility. Nothing in these files tells a beneficiary what their own denial is worth, and that is the piece the story supplies.

**Why pitch this now:** The threshold takes effect for requests filed on or after 01/01/27, so open enrollment season and year-end planning are the last window in which it is advice rather than history. The HCPCS Level II meeting is the second of two in 2026 and has registration instructions attached. The CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule comment record is fresh as of 09/15/26.

**Angle:** What does it now cost, in dollars and in filings, to contest a Medicare decision — and who is doing the contesting on behalf of people who will never file anything? Working title: "What It Costs to Argue With Medicare in 2027." For older adults and adult children handling denials, with a sidebar the trade can use on where coverage decisions are actually made.
